title: GPU stack upgrade playbook + Terraform module notes (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working draft playbook for performing coordinated upgrades of the GPU stack in Private deployments (VPC/on-prem). It combines a compatibility matrix, validation checklist, and notes about Terraform module changes we should land to make upgrades safer and repeatable.

Scope:
- Target environments: private (VPC) clusters and on-prem clusters managed by our platform package.
- Components covered: Kubernetes (kubelet/kubeadm), NVIDIA driver, CUDA toolkit (container driver compatibility), NCCL, containerd/CRI, GPU node kernel modules, and node-level OS packages that affect drivers.
- Not included: model runtime updates (LLM infra layer) unless they require new GPU features.

High-level upgrade approach (phases):
1) Preflight (automated checks + canary pool)
2) Driver/cuda upgrade on canary nodes (1-2 nodes)
3) Functional validation (smoke + perf) on canary
4) Gradual rollout by node pool (rolling drain/reboot)
5) Post-rollback window + full validation sweep

Compatibility matrix (summary - canonicalized as matrix for automation):
Columns: k8s-version | host-os | nvidia-driver | cuda-runtime | nccl | container-runtime | notes
- 1.26.x | ubuntu-22.04 | 535.104 | 12.2 | 2.18 | containerd-1.7 | baseline supported, requires kernel >= 5.15.0-80
- 1.25.x | ubuntu-22.04 | 525.85 | 11.8 | 2.12 | containerd-1.6 | stable, watch for kernel module rebuild on custom kernels
- 1.24.x | rhel-8.7 | 470.199 | 11.4 | 2.10 | docker-shim/containerd | legacy but in use for some air-gapped sites
- 1.27.x (alpha test) | ubuntu-24.04 | 545.50 | 13.0 | 2.20 | containerd-1.8 | experimental: requires updated nvidia-container-runtime and patched nvidia-uvm for vGPU feature

Key compatibility rules we enforce in validation harness: 
- NVIDIA driver major should be >= cuda-runtime major and within vendor-tested pairing. E.g., driver 525.x validated for CUDA 11.8 workloads; driver 535.x validated for 12.x.
- NCCL versions must match the CUDA ABI expectations of the container image (we pin NCCL minor in training containers).
- Kernel ABI breakages: any custom kernel builds must have DKMS-installed driver kernel modules; otherwise plan includes building drivers from source on nodes.

Validation checklist (automatable tasks first):
- Inventory: list nodes by pool, GPU model (A100, T4, V100), current driver, kernel, container runtime. Export to CSV.
- Backup cluster: snapshot etcd (if applicable) and store to S3-compatible store (link in linked_artifacts).
- Canary selection: choose pool with low traffic and representative GPU model. Flag it in TF with tag: "upgrade-canary".
- Terraform plan sanity: run 'terraform plan -target=module.node_pool.<canary>' and review diffs for node replacement vs in-place upgrade.
- Node-level preflight command (to run via ssh or agent):
  - nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,driver_version,pstate --format=csv
  - uname -r && lsb_release -a
  - containerd --version || dockerd --version
- Driver install smoke: after upgrade, verify 'nvidia-smi' returns correct driver and PCI devices visible.
- CUDA container validation: run a tiny CUDA vector-add container built against the target toolkit and verify GPU computation.
- NCCL ring test for multi-GPU nodes: run 'nccl-tests' or our lightweight collectives harness.
- K8s e2e smoke: schedule workload that uses device-plugin metrics and verify pod readiness + GPU allocation.
- Perf regression: run 1–3 representative inference/throughput tests and compare token latency and p99 throughput to baseline. Thresholds: <10% degradation p50, <15% degradation p99 or flag for rollback.

Terraform module notes (what to change to make upgrades safer):
- Add node_pool.lifecycle.replace_policy variable (options: replace, in_place, cordon-recreate) so we can choose node behavior per upgrade.
- Add tags for canary and last-upgraded-timestamp on instance metadata so automation can discover nodes quickly.
- Expose driver_install_strategy variable: pre-baked-image | cloud-init | daemonset. Default to daemonset for heterogeneous on-prem fleets.
- Support an "upgrade_plan" meta-object (string) that records the intended driver+cuda combo deployed by the module (useful for audits).
- Implement a terraform null_resource hook for running remote preflight/playbook scripts (idempotent) and make it opt-in.
- Add graceful-drain-timeout variable with sane defaults (e.g., 10m) and a pre-stop buffer for long-running inference GPUs.

Canary run template (sequence):
1) Tag selected node pool in TF and run terraform apply with replace_policy=cordon-recreate.
2) Wait for new nodes to join: kubectl get nodes --show-labels | grep upgrade-canary
3) Run node-level driver install (if daemonset strategy): kubectl apply -f nvidia-driver-daemonset.yaml --namespace kube-system --record
4) Smoke tests: nvidia-smi in pod context, run cuda-vector container, nccl-tests for multi-gpu
5) Run perf harness. If metrics pass, continue. If fail, revert terraform plan (trigger drain + rollback).

Rollback considerations: 
- If driver load fails on >30% of canary nodes, automatically rollback by triggering tf route that recreates nodes with previous AMI/image or old driver strategy.
- Keep previous driver packages cached in an internal repo for 14 days post-upgrade to allow quick re-install.
- Keep node-level logs (dmesg, /var/log/nvidia-installer.log, kubelet logs) collected to a temporary log bucket before destroying nodes.

Common failure modes and mitigations:
- Mismatched ABI leading to container SIGSEGV: ensure container rebuild against driver-compatible CUDA, use multi-stage tagging of images (cuda:11.8-cudnn8 -> runtime image).
- DKMS kernel module build failures: include kernel-devel package in node provisioning or prefer pre-baked images for on-prem.
- cloud-init race where container runtime not available when driver ds runs: add readiness probe for container runtime in driver ds.

Operational commands (quick reference):
- List GPUs and driver: kubectl run -it --rm --restart=Never --image=nvidia/cuda:11.8-base nvidia-check -- nvidia-smi
- Verify plugin registration: kubectl get pods -n kube-system | grep nvidia
- Collect logs from node: journalctl -u nvidia-docker -o short-iso | tail -n 200
- Reinstall driver (daemonset manual): kubectl rollout restart daemonset/nvidia-driver-daemonset -n kube-system

Testing artifacts and automation ideas:
- Add a CI job that applies the terraform module to a sandbox account with a mock node image and runs the validation harness.
- Use a matrix test runner that consumes the compatibility matrix as input and spins up ephemeral clusters (k3s / kind + mocked GPU device plugin) to validate kubelet + device plugin behaviors.
- Persist matrix as YAML in repo: infra/gpu/compat-matrix.yaml and version it with tags so upgrades reference a single source of truth.

Open questions (for follow-up):
- How do we want to handle mixed-GPU node pools during upgrade? Prefer pool-split or in-place upgrade?
- On air-gapped sites, should we require pre-baked AMIs/images as the default? (proposal: yes for safety).
- SLA windows: when can we schedule upgrades for enterprise customers with reserved capacity? Need product-ops input.

Next steps (action items):
- Diego: add replace_policy variable to terraform module (PR draft) — due 2024-12-01.
- Priya: build the small CUDA smoke image and add to internal registry (tag: smoke-cuda:11.8-test) — due 2024-12-05.
- Marcus: prototype CI sandbox runner for matrix-driven validation — due 2024-12-15.
- Amira (owner): consolidate this doc into a Confluence playbook, link the final compatibility YAML and the TF PRs — due 2025-01-10.

Appendix A: sample small test commands (copy-paste friendly)
- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,driver_version,memory.total --format=csv -L
- docker run --gpus all --rm nvidia/cuda:11.8-base nvidia-smi
- kubectl run cuda-smoke --image=registry.internal/smoke-cuda:11.8-test --limits='{"nvidia.com/gpu":1}' --restart=Never -- nvidia-smi

Appendix B: brief audit trail recommendation
- Store terraform plan outputs and apply logs in a per-customer artifact bucket.
- Tag each apply with upgrade-ticket (RDW-xxxx) and store driver package checksums in the upgrade metadata object.

End of draft.

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally pragmatic and operational — please comment inline with specific test thresholds or missing validation steps.
